================================================== Calculate business use %

Calculate business use %

Audit Binder – Notion Wiki TemplateVehicle Use
Checked
Client Task
Due Date@April 27, 2025
Notification
Priority LevelP3
Status
Not started
Task DescriptionTo satisfy the task for the audit documentation, follow these steps:

1.
Gather Data: Collect all relevant records that support your business use calculations. This may include invoices, receipts, and any relevant financial statements.

2.
Define Business Use: Clearly define what constitutes business use for your context. This can include the percentage of time a resource is used for business purposes versus personal use.

3.
Calculate Percentage: Use the formula:
\[
\text{Business Use \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Business Use Hours}}{\text{Total Hours}} \right) \times 100
\]
Ensure that you have accurate data on both business use hours and total hours.

4.
Document Findings: Create a clear and concise report that outlines your calculations, assumptions, and any supporting data. Include any pertinent details that an auditor may need.

5.
Review for Accuracy: Double-check your calculations and documentation to ensure everything is accurate and complete.

6.
Prepare for Audit: Organize your documentation in a way that is easy to navigate. Be prepared to explain your methodology and answer any questions from auditors.

Digital Binder Organization Guide

Duration: 3-4 minutes

Introduction (30 seconds)

Welcome to this tutorial on how to effectively organize your digital binder in Notion. This guide will help you structure and maintain your digital materials for final physical compilation.

Digital Tools Needed (15 seconds)

  • Notion workspace access
  • Digital files and documents
  • File naming system
  • Digital organization system

Step-by-Step Instructions (2 minutes)

  1. Set up your digital structureCreate clear categories and sections in Notion for different types of materials
  1. Establish naming conventionsUse consistent file names and organization patterns
  1. Maintain chronological orderKeep newest items easily accessible at the top of each section
  1. Ensure proper formattingVerify all documents are properly formatted for eventual printing
  1. Regular maintenanceKeep digital files organized and updated for final physical compilation

Common Digital Organization Mistakes (30 seconds)

  • Inconsistent file naming
  • Disorganized digital hierarchy
  • Missing or incomplete documentation
  • Poor version control

Closing (15 seconds)

A well-organized digital binder will make the final physical compilation process smooth and efficient. Thanks for watching!

Implementation Notes

  • Keep digital files properly categorized
  • Maintain consistent formatting across all documents
  • Regular backups of all materials
  • Track completion progress of each section

Purpose

To provide a clear, step-by-step overview of how to navigate and use this IRS audit packet.

Contents:

How to Use This Binder

  • Read through the Cover Page first.
  • Use the Table of Contents to locate each section.
  • Refer to the Exhibit Index for cross-referenced documentation.

Who Should Use This Packet

  • Taxpayers undergoing an IRS or state audit.
  • Tax preparers or representatives handling client audits.
  • Support teams gathering and submitting compliance documents.

Binder Section Overview

  • Each tabbed section contains specific documents relevant to audit categories (Income, Expenses, Payroll, etc.).
  • Subpages may be linked to external documents (Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.).
  • Every exhibit is labeled for easy navigation and reference.

Exhibit Index Navigation

  • Each exhibit is assigned a unique number and linked to the appropriate section.
  • Use the index to verify completeness, locate documents, or explain discrepancies.

Sensitive or Missing Documents

  • Any missing documents will be noted in the Audit Summary or Exhibit Notes.
  • Use your discretion to disclose gaps and explain them with context.

Contact Information

  • Prepared by: QiAlly – Cody Rice-Velasquez
  • Contact: cody@qially.me
⚠️ Reminder: This binder is intended for audit support. It does not substitute professional legal or tax defense in contentious audits. When in doubt, consult a tax attorney or enrolled agent.

Follow Up: After submission, monitor for any further communication from the IRS regarding the status of your response.

Calculate business use %To satisfy the task for the audit documentation, follow these steps:

1.
Gather Data: Collect all relevant records that support your business use calculations. This may include invoices, receipts, and any relevant financial statements.

2.
Define Business Use: Clearly define what constitutes business use for your context. This can include the percentage of time a resource is used for business purposes versus personal use.

3.
Calculate Percentage: Use the formula:
\[
\text{Business Use \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Business Use Hours}}{\text{Total Hours}} \right) \times 100
\]
Ensure that you have accurate data on both business use hours and total hours.

4.
Document Findings: Create a clear and concise report that outlines your calculations, assumptions, and any supporting data. Include any pertinent details that an auditor may need.

5.
Review for Accuracy: Double-check your calculations and documentation to ensure everything is accurate and complete.

Calculate business use %To satisfy the task for the audit documentation, follow these steps:

1.
Gather Data: Collect all relevant records that support your business use calculations. This may include invoices, receipts, and any relevant financial statements.

2.
Define Business Use: Clearly define what constitutes business use for your context. This can include the percentage of time a resource is used for business purposes versus personal use.

3.
Calculate Percentage: Use the formula:
\[
\text{Business Use \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Business Use Hours}}{\text{Total Hours}} \right) \times 100
\]
Ensure that you have accurate data on both business use hours and total hours.

4.
Document Findings: Create a clear and concise report that outlines your calculations, assumptions, and any supporting data. Include any pertinent details that an auditor may need.

5.
Review for Accuracy: Double-check your calculations and documentation to ensure everything is accurate and complete.

6.
Prepare for Audit: Organize your documentation in a way that is easy to navigate. Be prepared to explain your methodology and answer any questions from auditors.		P3Vehicle UseVehicle Use

Measure full home square footage + office spaceTo satisfy the task for the audit documentation, follow these steps:

1.
Gather Tools: Obtain a measuring tape or a laser measuring device to ensure accuracy.
2.
Measure Each Room: Measure the length and width of each room in the home, including hallways, closets, and the office space. Record these measurements.
3.
Calculate Square Footage: For each room, multiply the length by the width to get the square footage.
4.
Total the Measurements: Add together the square footage of all rooms to obtain the full home square footage.
5.
Document Findings: Create a detailed report including the measurements, calculations, and total square footage. Ensure that this document is clear and organized for audit purposes.
6.
Review and Submit: Double-check all calculations for accuracy before submitting the documentation.

Make sure to keep a copy of all notes and calculations for future reference.

Calculate business use %To satisfy the task for the audit documentation, follow these steps:

1.
Gather Data: Collect all relevant records that support your business use calculations. This may include invoices, receipts, and any relevant financial statements.

2.
Define Business Use: Clearly define what constitutes business use for your context. This can include the percentage of time a resource is used for business purposes versus personal use.

3.
Calculate Percentage: Use the formula:
\[
\text{Business Use \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Business Use Hours}}{\text{Total Hours}} \right) \times 100
\]
Ensure that you have accurate data on both business use hours and total hours.

4.
Document Findings: Create a clear and concise report that outlines your calculations, assumptions, and any supporting data. Include any pertinent details that an auditor may need.

5.
Review for Accuracy: Double-check your calculations and documentation to ensure everything is accurate and complete.

Calculate business use %To satisfy the task for the audit documentation, follow these steps:

1.
Gather Data: Collect all relevant records that support your business use calculations. This may include invoices, receipts, and any relevant financial statements.

2.
Define Business Use: Clearly define what constitutes business use for your context. This can include the percentage of time a resource is used for business purposes versus personal use.

3.
Calculate Percentage: Use the formula:
\[
\text{Business Use \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Business Use Hours}}{\text{Total Hours}} \right) \times 100
\]
Ensure that you have accurate data on both business use hours and total hours.

4.
Document Findings: Create a clear and concise report that outlines your calculations, assumptions, and any supporting data. Include any pertinent details that an auditor may need.
